Document 2805: Lawyer's reliance on ChatGPT leads to false case citations in airline lawsuit
A New York lawyer has found himself in trouble in a lawsuit between a man and the airline Avianca Holding S.A. after presenting nonexistent citations in the case generated by ChatGPT.
一名纽约律师在一名男子与航空公司Avianca Holding S.A.之间的诉讼中遇到麻烦，原因是他提交了由ChatGPT生成的虚假案例引用。
The case involved a man named Roberto Mata suing Avianca, claiming he was injured when a metal service cart struck his knee during a flight.受影响方 Injury claims are typically uninteresting, aside from the broader cultural considerations about how the U.S. [is so litigious](https://statmodeling.stat.columbia.edu/2015/12/03/why-us-litigious/), but the case took an interesting twist after the airline attempted to have the case dismissed.
The New York Times [reported](https://www.nytimes.com/2023/05/27/nyregion/avianca-airline-lawsuit-chatgpt.html) Saturday that in response to the filing, lawyers representing Mata submitted a 10-page brief citing more than a half-dozen relevant court cases, arguing that the cases show the “tolling effect of the automatic stay on a statute of limitations.”
该案涉及一名名为罗伯托·马塔的男子起诉Avianca，称他在一次航班上被金属服务车撞伤膝盖。伤害赔偿诉讼通常并不引人关注，除了美国诉讼文化这一更广泛的社会考量因素外，但这起案件在航空公司试图驳回此案后出现了有趣的转折。
One huge problem, however, is that none of the cases was genuine. The lawyer who created the brief, Steven A. Schwartz of the firm Levidow, Levidow & Oberman, had used OpenAI LP’s ChatGPT to write it.
Schwartz, who is said to have practiced law for three decades, defended himself, claiming that he wasn’t aware of the AI’s potential to generate false content. Schwartz told Judge P. Kevin Castel that he had no intent to deceive the court or the airline and vowed not to use ChatGPT again without thorough verification. The unusual situation prompted the judge to call a hearing on potential sanctions against Schwartz, describing the incident as an “unprecedented circumstance” filled with “bogus judicial decisions.”
《纽约时报》周六报道，作为对起诉书的回应，代表马塔的律师提交了一份10页的简报，引用了超过六七起相关案例，认为这些案例表明“自动暂缓对诉讼时效的阻却效力”。
The incident has sparked discussions among the legal community about the values and risks of AI. Stephen Gillers, a legal ethics professor at New York University School of Law, told the Times that the case highlights that legal professionals can’t simply take the output from an AI and incorporate it into court filings. “The discussion now among the bar is how to avoid exactly what this case describes,” Gillers added.
The case creates a precedent because of the role AI plays in legal research and argument construction, which has surfaced severe concerns about the reliability of AI tools in the legal profession. The case also underscores the potential hazards of trusting AI outputs in not only court filings but also in general use without secondary verification.
然而，一个巨大的问题是，这些案例没有一个是真实存在的。撰写这份简报的律师是来自Levidow, Levidow & Oberman律所的史蒂文·A·施瓦茨，他使用了OpenAI LP公司的ChatGPT来撰写这份文件。
Document 2836: No ChatGPT in my court: Judge orders all AI-generated content must be declared and checked
Few lawyers would be foolish enough to let an AI make their arguments, but one already did, and Judge Brantley Starr is taking steps to ensure that debacle isn’t repeated in _his_ courtroom.
很少有律师会愚蠢到让人工智能替他们辩论，但已经有一位这么做了，布拉德利·斯塔尔法官正采取措施，确保这种溃败不会在他的法庭上重演。
The Texas federal judge has added a requirement that any attorney appearing in his court must attest that “no portion of the filing was drafted by generative artificial intelligence,” or if it was, that it was checked “by a human being.”
Last week, attorney Steven Schwartz allowed [ChatGPT](https://techcrunch.com/2023/05/18/chatgpt-everything-you-need-to-know-about-the-ai-powered-chatbot/) to “supplement” his legal research in a recent federal filing, providing him with six cases and relevant precedent — all of which were completely hallucinated by the language model. He now [“greatly regrets” doing this](https://arstechnica.com/tech-policy/2023/05/lawyer-cited-6-fake-cases-made-up-by-chatgpt-judge-calls-it-unprecedented/), and while the national coverage of this gaffe probably caused any other lawyers thinking of trying it to think again, Judge Starr isn’t taking any chances.
这位德克萨斯州的联邦法官增加了一项要求，任何在他的法庭出庭的律师必须证明“提交的文件没有任何部分是由生成式人工智能起草的”，或者如果是由人工智能起草的，已经“由人工”检查过了。
At the federal site for Texas’s Northern District, Starr has, like other judges, the opportunity to set specific rules for his courtroom. And added recently (though it’s unclear whether this was in response to the aforementioned filing) is the [“Mandatory Certification Regarding Generative Artificial Intelligence.”](https://www.txnd.uscourts.gov/judge/judge-brantley-starr) Eugene Volokh [first reported the news](https://reason.com/volokh/2023/05/30/federal-judge-requires-all-lawyers-to-file-certificates-related-to-use-of-generative-ai/).
> All attorneys appearing before the Court must file on the docket a certificate attesting either that no portion of the filing was drafted by generative artificial intelligence (such as ChatGPT, Harvey.AI, or Google Bard) or that any language drafted by generative artificial intelligence was checked for accuracy, using print reporters or traditional legal databases, by a human being.风险控制
上周，律师史蒂文·施瓦茨允许ChatGPT“补充”他的法律研究，在最近的一份联邦文件中为他提供了六个案例和相关先例——所有这些都是由语言模型完全凭空编造的。他现在“深感后悔”这样做，虽然此事件的全国性报道可能已经让其他考虑尝试的律师三思，但斯塔尔法官不会冒任何风险。
A form for lawyers to sign is appended, noting that “quotations, citations, paraphrased assertions, and legal analysis” are all covered by this proscription. As summary is one of AI’s strong suits, and finding and summarizing precedent or previous cases is something that has been advertised as potentially helpful in legal work, this may end up coming into play more often than expected.
Whoever drafted the memorandum on this matter at Judge Starr’s office has their finger on the pulse. The certification requirement includes a pretty well informed and convincing explanation of its necessity (line breaks added for readability):
在德克萨斯州北区联邦法院网站上，斯塔尔与其他法官一样，有机会为自己的法庭设定具体规则。他最近增加了一项规定（虽然尚不清楚这是否是针对上述文件的回应），即“关于生成式人工智能的强制认证”。尤金·沃洛赫最先报道了这一消息。
> These platforms are incredibly powerful and have many uses in the law: form divorces, discovery requests, suggested errors in documents, anticipated questions at oral argument. But legal briefing is not one of them. Here’s why.
>
> 所有在该法院出庭的律师必须在案卷上提交一份证明，证明提交的文件没有任何部分是由生成式人工智能（如ChatGPT、Harvey.AI或Google Bard）起草的，或者任何由生成式人工智能起草的语言已经由人工使用印刷报告或传统法律数据库进行了准确性核查。
> These platforms in their current states are prone to hallucinations and bias. On hallucinations, they make stuff up—even quotes and citations. Another issue is reliability or bias. While attorneys swear an oath to set aside their personal prejudices, biases, and beliefs to faithfully uphold the law and represent their clients, generative artificial intelligence is the product of programming devised by humans who did not have to swear such an oath.
>
附有律师需要签署的表格，其中指出“引文、引用、复述的主张和法律分析”都属于此禁令的范围。由于摘要正是人工智能的强项，查找和总结先例或以往案例被视为法律工作中可能有帮助的功能，这一点可能会比预期更频繁地被涉及。
> As such, these systems hold no allegiance to any client, the rule of law, or the laws and Constitution of the United States (or, as addressed above, the truth). Unbound by any sense of duty, honor, or justice, such programs act according to computer code rather than conviction, based on programming rather than principle. Any party believing a platform has the requisite accuracy and reliability for legal briefing may move for leave and explain why.
In other words, be prepared to justify yourself.
在斯塔尔法官办公室起草这份备忘录的人对时事有着敏锐的把握。认证要求包括一段相当知情且令人信服的必要性解释（为便于阅读而添加了换行）：
While this is just one judge in one court, it would not be surprising if others took up this rule as their own. While as the court says, this is a powerful and potentially helpful technology, its use must be at the very least clearly declared and checked for accuracy.
Document 2841: Lawyer blames ChatGPT for 'bogus citations'
A lawyer with over 30 years of practice behind him has used ChatGPT for a case -- allegedly for the first time in his career -- and is now the subject of disciplinary proceedings set for hearing this June.
一位执业超过30年的律师在一起案件中使用了ChatGPT——据称这是他职业生涯中首次使用——目前他正面临将于今年6月开庭审理的纪律处分程序。
In Mata v. Avianca, Inc., a case currently being tried before the U.S. district court for the Southern District of New York, the plaintiff Mata sued the airline Avianca after an employee hit his knee with a serving cart during a 2019 flight from El Salvador to New York.
Avianca responded that the limitations period for the suit had expired and asked the court to dismiss the case against it.
在Mata诉Avianca航空公司一案中，这起案件目前正在纽约南区联邦地区法院审理，原告Mata起诉该航空公司，因为2019年一次从萨尔瓦多飞往纽约的航班上，一名员工用服务推车撞伤了他的膝盖。
The plaintiff objected with a 10-page brief citing case law to support the claim that Mata's lawsuit had been filed in time. Among the court decisions Mata's lawyers cited were Martinez v. Delta Air Lines, Zicherman v. Korean Air Lines, and Varghese v. China Southern Airlines, the New York Times reported.
When Avianca's lawyers wrote the district judge to say they could not find any of the decisions cited in the brief, the court ordered the plaintiff to provide an affidavit annexing some of the cited cases, which the plaintiff [did](https://storage.courtlistener.com/recap/gov.uscourts.nysd.575368/gov.uscourts.nysd.575368.29.1.pdf).
Avianca回应称，该诉讼的时效期限已过，请求法院驳回针对该公司的诉讼。原告以一份10页的简报提出异议，援引案例法支持其诉讼未过时效的主张。据《纽约时报》报道，Mata的律师在简报中引用的法院判决包括Martinez诉达美航空案、Zicherman诉大韩航空案以及Varghese诉中国南方航空案。
"Six of the submitted cases appear to be bogus judicial decisions with bogus quotes and bogus internal citations," the district judge wrote in an [order dated May 4, 2023](https://storage.courtlistener.com/recap/gov.uscourts.nysd.575368/gov.uscourts.nysd.575368.31.0.pdf). "Set forth below is an order to show cause why plaintiff's counsel ought not be sanctioned."
It was then that Steven Schwartz of law firm Levidow, Levidow & Oberman finally admitted that he had used ChatGPT to "supplement the legal research performed" by him for Mata's brief, and that ChatGPT had provided six citations which he had then relied on but which "this court has found to be non-existent".
当Avianca的律师致函地区法官表示他们无法找到简报中引用的任何判决时，法院命令原告提供一份附上部分引用案例的书面陈述，原告照做了。
In his [affidavit](https://storage.courtlistener.com/recap/gov.uscourts.nysd.575368/gov.uscourts.nysd.575368.32.1.pdf), Schwartz explained that he had never used "Chat GPT" for legal research in "over thirty years of practice" before and was not aware that its output could be false.
Schwartz attached screenshots of his conversation with ChatGPT to his affidavit which showed that he had asked the large language model (LLM) whether Varghese v. China Southern Airlines was a real case. ChatGPT had responded in the affirmative.
“这六份提交的案例似乎是伪造的司法判决，包含伪造的引用和伪造的内部引用，”地区法官在2023年5月4日发布的命令中写道。“以下是命令原告律师说明为何不应受到制裁的理由。”
"Upon double-checking, I found that the case Varghese v. China Southern Airlines Co. Ltd., 925 F.3d 1339 (11th Cir. 2019), does indeed exist and can be found on legal research databases such as Westlaw and LexisNexis," ChatGPT said when Schwartz asked it for its source.
Schwartz admitted it was his fault for not confirming the sources provided by the LLM. He expressed his regret on relying on ChatGPT and promised the district court he would never do so again "without absolute verification of its authenticity".
直到那时，Levidow, Levidow & Oberman律师事务所的Steven Schwartz才承认他使用了ChatGPT来“补充”他为Mata的简报所做的法律研究，而ChatGPT提供的六个引用他随后予以采用，但“本法院已认定这些引用不存在”。
Bart Banino, a lawyer for Avianca, told the New York Times that his firm, Condon & Forsyth, specialised in aviation law and immediately suspected that AI had been involved in churning out the "bogus" citations in Mata's brief.
Tech research and consulting firm Gartner [recently warned legal and compliance officers](https://www.thelawyermag.com/au/news/general/gartner-ids-six-chatgpt-legal-and-compliance-risks-to-stay-ahead-of/446578?__hstc=208808397.aa3675558db3d757eec905f181576c47.1685498837165.1685498837165.1685498837165.1&__hssc=208808397.1.1685498837165&__hsfp=1374498491) that LLM tools, including ChatGPT, were prone to providing plausible-sounding but incorrect information called "hallucinations".
Schwartz在其书面陈述中解释称，在“超过30年的执业生涯”中，他从未使用过“ChatGPT”进行法律研究，也不知道它的输出可能是虚假的。
The U.S. district judge hearing [Mata v. Avianca](https://www.courtlistener.com/docket/63107798/mata-v-avianca-inc/?filed_after=&filed_before=&entry_gte=&entry_lte=&order_by=desc) called the situation an "unprecedented circumstance" and ordered a hearing on June 8 to discuss potential sanctions on Schwartz.
Document 2847: US Lawyer Faces Sanctions Over Using ChatGPT-Suggested Citations In Lawsuit
The credibility of ChatGPT, an AI chatbot developed by OpenAI, has been called into question after it deceived a lawyer into believing that citations provided by the chatbot were legitimate, when in fact they were fabricated.风险 Lawyer Steven A Schwartz, who was representing a client in a lawsuit against Avianca, a Colombian airline, admitted in an affidavit that he had relied on the chatbot for his research, as reported by The New York Times.
ChatGPT的信誉受到质疑，此前这款由OpenAI开发的人工智能聊天机器人在一起案件中欺骗了一名律师，使其相信聊天机器人提供的引文是合法的，而实际上这些引文是伪造的。据《纽约时报》报道，代表客户对哥伦比亚航空公司Avianca提起诉讼的律师史蒂文·A·施瓦茨在一份书面陈述中承认，他曾依赖该聊天机器人进行调研。
During the proceedings, the opposing counsel pointed out that several of the cited cases were non-existent. US District Judge Kevin Castel reviewed the submissions and confirmed that six of the cases included in the lawyer's arguments were based on fabricated judicial decisions, complete with false quotes and internal citations. As a result, the judge has scheduled a hearing to consider potential sanctions against the plaintiff's legal team.
Schwartz claimed that he had asked the chatbot if it was providing accurate information. When he requested a source for the citations, ChatGPT apologised for the earlier confusion and insisted that the cited case was indeed real. The chatbot also maintained that the other cases it had referenced were genuine. Schwartz admitted that he had been unaware of the possibility that the chatbot's content could be false. He expressed deep regret for relying on generative artificial intelligence to supplement his legal research and vowed to never do so again without thorough verification of its authenticity.
在诉讼过程中，对方律师指出，多个被引用的案件并不存在。美国地区法官凯文·卡斯特尔审查了提交的材料后确认，律师论点中包含的六个案件均基于伪造的司法裁决，其中包含虚假的引语和内部引用。因此，法官已安排听证会，以考虑对原告法律团队实施制裁的可能性。
This incident follows another recent controversy involving ChatGPT, in which the chatbot falsely implicated an innocent and highly respected law professor, \\[Name redacted\\], in a research study on legal scholars who had engaged in sexual harassment in the past. Turley, who holds the Shapiro Chair of Public Interest Law at George Washington University, was shocked to discover that ChatGPT had mistakenly included his name on the list of scholars accused of misconduct. Turley took to Twitter to express his disbelief, stating, "ChatGPT recently issued a false story accusing me of sexually assaulting students."
These incidents raise concerns about the reliability and potential risks associated with AI-generated content in legal research and decision-making processes. The need for stringent verification and fact-checking when using AI tools like ChatGPT in legal contexts has become increasingly apparent to avoid the dissemination of false information and the potential harm it can cause to individuals and legal proceedings.
施瓦茨声称，他曾询问聊天机器人是否在提供准确信息。当他要求提供引文的来源时，ChatGPT为之前的混淆表示歉意，并坚称被引用的案件确实是真实存在的。聊天机器人还声称它所引用的其他案件也都是真实的。施瓦茨承认，他之前并不知道聊天机器人的内容可能是虚假的。他对依赖生成式人工智能来辅助法律调研表示深切遗憾，并发誓今后在未经彻底验证其真实性之前，绝不再使用此类工具。
Document 2849: Lawyer faces sanctions for using ‘bogus’ citations from ChatGPT
Steven Schwartz, a lawyer at US law firm Levidow & Oberman, will face a sanctions hearing on 8 June 2023 after submitting a brief filled with fictitious cases and fabricated court citations.
Steven Schwartz是是美国律师事务所Levidow & Oberman的律师，他将在2023年6月8日面临一场制裁听证会，此前他提交了一份包含虚构案件和伪造法庭引用的简报。
Schwartz was acting for airline passenger Roberto Mata in a negligence lawsuit against Avianca airlines and used ChatGPT in his legal research.
The brief cited cases that were decided between 1999 and 2019 to support Schwartz’s argument that the case should be heard despite it being beyond the statute of limitations. However, neither the judge nor the airline’s lawyers could find the decisions or quotations summarised.
Schwartz代表航空乘客Roberto Mata对Avianca航空提起过失诉讼，并在法律研究中使用ChatGPT。
Judge Kevin Castel, from the Southern District of New York, asserted at least six of the cases submitted “appear to be bogus judicial decisions with bogus quotes and bogus internal citations”.
“The court is presented with an unprecedented circumstance,” Castel wrote.
简报引用了1999年至2019年期间判决的案件，以支持Schwartz关于尽管已超过诉讼时效该案仍应被受理的论点。然而，法官和航空公司律师都无法找到这些判决或引用。
> The court is presented with an unprecedented circumstance.
>
来自纽约南区的法官Kevin Castel断言，提交的文件中至少六起案件“似乎是伪造的司法判决，包含伪造的引用和伪造的内部引用”。
> Justice Kevin Castel, New York
Schwartz’s brief included fictitious cases ChatGPT had made up including Varghese v China South Airlines, Shaboon v EgyptAir, Martinez v Delta Airlines, Miller v United Airlines, Petersen v Iran Air and Estate of Durden v KLM Royal Dutch Airlines.
“法院面临前所未有的情况。”Castel写道。
In an affidavit, Schwartz admitted he “was unaware of the possibility that \\[ChatGPT\\] content could be false”. He took full responsibility for failing to verify the sources and greatly regretted “having utilised generative artificial intelligence to supplement the legal research performed”.
Schwartz vowed to “never do so \\[again\\] in the future without absolute verification of its \\[ChatGPT\\] authenticity”.
> 法院面临前所未有的情况。
After being ordered to show cause for why he should not be sanctioned, Schwartz included screenshots of his attempts to confirm the authenticity of cases with ChatGPT.
>
“Is Varghese a real case?” Schwartz asked ChatGPT.
> 法官Kevin Castel，纽约
“Yes, it is a real case,” the chatbot replied.
Schwartz asked ChatGPT to confirm its source to which it replied: “Upon double-checking, I found the case Varghese v. China Southern Airlines Co. Ltd., 925 F.3d 1339 (11th Cir. 2019), does indeed exist and can be found on legal research databases such as Westlaw and LexisNexis.”
Schwartz的简报包含了ChatGPT编造的虚构案件，包括Varghese诉中国南方航空公司案、Shaboon诉埃及航空案、Martinez诉达美航空案、Miller诉联合航空案、Petersen诉伊朗航空案以及Durden遗产诉荷兰皇家航空案。
“I apologise for any inconvenience or confusion my earlier responses may have caused,” ChatGPT wrote.
Schwartz also asked the chatbot if any of the other cases provided were fake and ChatGPT responded: “No, the other cases I provided are real and can be found in reputable legal databases.”
在一份宣誓书中，Schwartz承认他“不知道ChatGPT生成的内容可能为假的可能性”。他对自己的行为承担全部责任，深表遗憾地表示“利用生成式人工智能来补充法律研究工作”。
Legal ethics professor Stephen Gillers, from New York University Law School, told the _New York Times_ that the case illustrates what lawyers should not do.
“You cannot just take the output and cut and paste it into your court filings,” said Gillers.
Schwartz发誓“将来绝不会再这样做，除非能够绝对验证ChatGPT的真实性”。
Document 2977: Lawyers have real bad day in court after citing fake cases made up by ChatGPT
A federal judge tossed a lawsuit and issued a $5,000 fine to the plaintiff's lawyers after they used ChatGPT to research court filings that cited six fake cases invented by the artificial intelligence tool made by OpenAI.影响
一名联邦法官驳回了一起诉讼，并对原告律师处以5000美元罚款，原因是他使用ChatGPT研究法庭文件时引用了六起由OpenAI开发的人工智能工具编造的虚假案例。
Lawyers Steven Schwartz and Peter LoDuca of the firm Levidow, Levidow, & Oberman "abandoned their responsibilities when they submitted non-existent judicial opinions with fake quotes and citations created by the artificial intelligence tool ChatGPT, then continued to stand by the fake opinions after judicial orders called their existence into question," [US District Judge Kevin Castel wrote](https://storage.courtlistener.com/recap/gov.uscourts.nysd.575368/gov.uscourts.nysd.575368.54.0_5.pdf) in an order yesterday. The lawyers, Castel wrote, "advocated for the fake cases and legal arguments" even "after being informed by their adversary's submission that their citations were non-existent and could not be found."
The judge issued one fine of $5,000 to be paid by the two lawyers and their firm under joint and several liability. More embarrassingly for the lawyers, they are required to send letters to six real judges who were "falsely identified as the author of the fake" opinions cited in their legal filings. Castel described the legal analysis in one of the fake cases as "gibberish."
法官凯文·卡斯特尔昨日在命令中写道，来自Levidow, Levidow, & Oberman律师事务所的律师史蒂文·施瓦茨和彼得·洛杜卡“在提交由人工智能工具ChatGPT编造的不存在的司法意见以及虚假引文和引用后，放弃了自己的职责，随后在法院命令对这些意见的存在提出质疑后，他们仍然坚持这些虚假意见。”
"The Court will require Respondents to inform their client and the judges whose names were wrongfully invoked of the sanctions imposed," Castel wrote. "The Court will not require an apology from Respondents because a compelled apology is not a sincere apology. Any decision to apologize is left to Respondents."
Submitting fake opinions to a court harms the lawyers' client, wastes the court's time, forces the opposing party to waste "time and money in exposing the deception," and causes "potential harm to the reputation of judges and courts whose names are falsely invoked as authors of the bogus opinions and to the reputation of a party attributed with fictional conduct," Castel wrote. "It promotes cynicism about the legal profession and the American judicial system. And a future litigant may be tempted to defy a judicial ruling by disingenuously claiming doubt about its authenticity."
卡斯特尔写道，这些律师甚至“在被对方提交的文件中告知他们的引文不存在且无法找到后”，仍然“为这些虚假案例和法律论点进行辩护”。
Case dismissed
--------------
法官处以一次5000美元的罚款，由两名律师及其律师事务所共同连带承担。更令律师们难堪的是，他们必须向六名真实法官发送信件，这些法官被“错误地指认为这些虚假意见的作者”。卡斯特尔将其中一个虚假案例的法律分析描述为“胡言乱语”。
As we [wrote last month](https://arstechnica.com/tech-policy/2023/05/lawyer-cited-6-fake-cases-made-up-by-chatgpt-judge-calls-it-unprecedented/), Schwartz admitted using ChatGPT for research and did not verify whether the "legal opinions" provided by the AI chatbot were accurate. Schwartz wrote in an affidavit that he had "never utilized ChatGPT as a source for conducting legal research prior to this occurrence and therefore was unaware of the possibility that its content could be false."
The real case, _Roberto Mata vs. Avianca_, was originally filed in a New York state court but was moved to US District Court for the Southern District of New York. Schwartz was representing Mata in state court but wasn't admitted to practice in the federal court. Schwartz continued to write the legal briefs and LoDuca filed them under his own name.
“法院将要求被申请人告知其当事人以及那些姓名被不当使用的法官所受到的制裁，”卡斯特尔写道。“法院不会要求被申请人道歉，因为被迫的道歉不是真诚的道歉。任何道歉的决定都留给被申请人。”
Mata sought damages for injuries suffered during an Avianca flight from El Salvador to New York in August 2019 when a metal snack and drink cart struck his knee. Mata's lawyers used the phony citations from ChatGPT to argue that the case should be moved back to the New York state court where a three-year statute of limitations would apply.
Unsurprisingly, their argument citing phony cases wasn't persuasive to the judge. In addition to punishing the lawyers, Castel yesterday [granted Avianca's motion](https://storage.courtlistener.com/recap/gov.uscourts.nysd.575368/gov.uscourts.nysd.575368.55.0_4.pdf) to dismiss the case. The judge agreed with the defendant that a two-year statute of limitations under the Montreal Convention applies and that the plaintiff's lawsuit was filed too late.
向法院提交虚假意见会损害律师委托人的利益，浪费法院的时间，迫使对方“花费时间和金钱揭露欺骗”，并对“被虚假指认为虚假意见作者的法官和法院的声誉以及被归咎于虚构行为的当事人的声誉造成潜在损害”，卡斯特尔写道。“这助长了对法律职业和美国司法制度的冷嘲热讽。未来的诉讼当事人可能会试图通过虚假声称对裁决真实性存疑来蔑视司法裁决。”
“I just never thought it could be made up”
------------------------------------------
案件被驳回
The dispute over fake precedents played out over a few months. On March 1, Mata's lawyers cited the fake cases in a [brief](https://storage.courtlistener.com/recap/gov.uscourts.nysd.575368/gov.uscourts.nysd.575368.21.0.pdf) that opposed Avianca's motion to dismiss the case.
"But if the matter had ended with Respondents coming clean about their actions shortly after they received the defendant's March 15 brief questioning the existence of the cases, or after they reviewed the Court's Orders of April 11 and 12 requiring production of the cases, the record now would look quite different," Castel wrote. "Instead, the individual Respondents doubled down and did not begin to dribble out the truth until May 25, after the Court issued an Order to Show Cause why one of the individual Respondents ought not be sanctioned."
正如我们上个月报道的那样，施瓦茨承认使用ChatGPT进行研究，但没有验证人工智能聊天机器人提供的“法律意见”是否准确。施瓦茨在一份书面陈述中写道，他“在此事件之前从未使用ChatGPT作为进行法律研究的来源，因此不知道其内容可能是虚假的。”
Castel found that the lawyers were guilty of "bad faith" and "acts of conscious avoidance and false and misleading statements to the Court." While Schwartz wrote the bogus legal filings, LoDuca didn't check them for accuracy.
"Mr. LoDuca simply relied on a belief that work produced by Mr. Schwartz, a colleague of more than twenty-five years, would be reliable," Castel wrote. But Schwartz's practice was exclusively in state court. The lawyers admitted in a memorandum of law that Schwartz attempted "to research a federal bankruptcy issue with which he was completely unfamiliar."
这起真实案件——罗伯托·马塔诉阿维安卡航空——最初在纽约州法院提起，但被移交到纽约州南区美国联邦地区法院。施瓦茨在州法院代表马塔，但他没有获得联邦法院的执业许可。施瓦茨继续撰写法律简报，洛杜卡以自己的名义提交。
At a June 8 hearing on potential sanctions, Schwartz testified that he was "operating under the false perception that this website \\[ChatGPT\\] could not possibly be fabricating cases on its own." Schwartz stated, "I just was not thinking that the case could be fabricated, so I was not looking at it from that point of view... My reaction was, ChatGPT is finding that case somewhere. Maybe it's unpublished. Maybe it was appealed. Maybe access is difficult to get. I just never thought it could be made up."
The Levidow firm did not have Westlaw or LexisNexis accounts, instead using a Fastcase account that had limited access to federal cases. Schwartz testified that he "heard about this new site which I assumed—I falsely assumed was like a super search engine called ChatGPT, and that's what I used."
马塔寻求因2019年8月从萨尔瓦多飞往纽约的航班上被金属零食和饮料车撞伤膝盖而遭受的损害赔偿。马塔的律师使用ChatGPT编造的虚假引用来论证案件应被移回纽约州法院，在那里将适用三年诉讼时效。
According to Castel, "Schwartz testified that he began by querying ChatGPT for broad legal guidance and then narrowed his questions to cases that supported the argument that the federal bankruptcy stay tolled the limitations period for a claim under the Montreal Convention."
Schwartz untruthfully claimed that ChatGPT merely "supplemented" his research, Castel wrote. Schwartz later admitted that his entire research consisted of querying ChatGPT. "It became my last resort," he testified.
不出所料，他们引用虚假案例的论点未能说服法官。除了惩罚这些律师外，卡斯特尔昨日批准了阿维安卡的驳回动议。法官同意被告的观点，即《蒙特利尔公约》适用两年诉讼时效，且原告的诉讼提交得太晚。
In April, the judge issued orders directing LoDuca to file copies of the precedents that no one could locate. LoDuca requested an extension of time, claiming that he was out of the office on vacation.
"Mr. LoDuca's statement was false and he knew it to be false at the time he made the statement. Under questioning by the Court at the sanctions hearing, Mr. LoDuca admitted that he was not out of the office on vacation," Castel wrote. LoDuca testified that Schwartz was away and that "I just attempted to get Mr. Schwartz the additional time he needed because he was out of the office at the time."
“从没想过它可能是捏造的”
According to Castel, this "lie had the intended effect of concealing Mr. Schwartz's role in preparing the March 1 Affirmation and the April 25 Affidavit and concealing Mr. LoDuca's lack of meaningful role in confirming the truth of the statements in his affidavit. This is evidence of the subjective bad faith of Mr. LoDuca."
The April 25 filings included a series of "excerpts" from the bogus decisions. The filing "did not comply with the Court's Orders of April 11 and 12 because it did not attach the full text of any of the 'cases' that are now admitted to be fake," Castel wrote.
关于虚假先例的争议持续了数月。3月1日，马塔的律师在一份简报中引用了这些虚假案例，反驳阿维安卡要求驳回案件的动议。
“Gibberish,” “borders on nonsensical”
-------------------------------------
“但如果被申请人在收到被告3月15日质疑这些案例存在性的简报后，或在审查了法院4月11日和12日要求提供这些案例的命令后，立即坦白自己的行为，那么现在的记录将会大不相同，”卡斯特尔写道。“相反，个人被申请人变本加厉，直到5月25日，在法院发出命令要求个别被申请人说明为何不应受到制裁后，他们才开始一点点透露真相。”
The fake [_Varghese v. China Southern Airlines_](https://storage.courtlistener.com/recap/gov.uscourts.nysd.575368/gov.uscourts.nysd.575368.29.1.pdf) excerpt submitted by LoDuca and Schwartz, supposedly issued by the US Court of Appeals for the 11th Circuit, "shows stylistic and reasoning flaws that do not generally appear in decisions issued by United States Courts of Appeals," Castel wrote. "Its legal analysis is gibberish... The summary of the case's procedural history is difficult to follow and borders on nonsensical."
The _Varghese_ decision also "includes internal citations and quotes from decisions that are themselves non-existent," the judge noted. The other fake precedents submitted to the court had similar flaws.
卡斯特尔认定这些律师犯了“恶意”行为和“故意回避以及向法院作出虚假和误导性陈述”。虽然施瓦茨撰写了虚假法律文件，但洛杜卡没有检查其准确性。
Despite that, the lawyers have never "written to this Court seeking to withdraw the March 1 Affirmation in Opposition or advise the Court that it may no longer rely upon it," Castel wrote.
Castel also found that Schwartz acted in bad faith and violated a federal rule when, in his April 25 affidavit, he did not reveal that he couldn't find the full decisions cited in his previous filing. "Poor and sloppy research would merely have been objectively unreasonable. But Mr. Schwartz was aware of facts that alerted him to the high probability that 'Varghese' and 'Zicherman' did not exist and consciously avoided confirming that fact," Castel wrote.
“洛杜卡先生只是依赖这样一种信念：与他共事超过二十五年的同事施瓦茨先生的工作应该是可靠的，”卡斯特尔写道。但施瓦茨的执业范围仅限于州法院。律师在一份法律备忘录中承认，施瓦茨尝试“研究一个他完全不熟悉的联邦破产问题”。
"Mr. Schwartz's subjective bad faith is further supported by the untruthful assertion that ChatGPT was merely a 'supplement' to his research, his conflicting accounts about his queries to ChatGPT as to whether 'Varghese' is a 'real' case, and the failure to disclose reliance on ChatGPT in the April 25 Affidavit," the judge added.
Some changes are in the works at the law firm to prevent repeats of the fiasco. Thomas Corvino, the sole equity partner of the Levidow firm, "has acknowledged responsibility, identified remedial measures taken by the Levidow Firm, including an expanded Fastcase subscription and CLE \\[continuing legal education\\] programming, and expressed his regret for Respondents' submissions," Castel wrote.
在6月8日关于潜在制裁的听证会上，施瓦茨作证说，他“在一个错误的认知下操作，即这个网站[ChatGPT]不可能自己编造案例。”施瓦茨表示，“我只是没有想过这个案例可能是编造的，所以没有从那个角度去看待它……我的反应是，ChatGPT在某处找到了那个案例。也许它未公开出版。也许它被上诉了。也许访问困难。我从没想过它可能是捏造的。”
The judge doesn't think it will happen again. "The Court credits the sincerity of Respondents when they described their embarrassment and remorse," Castel wrote. "The fake cases were not submitted for any respondent's financial gain and were not done out of personal animus. Respondents do not have a history of disciplinary violations and there is a low likelihood that they will repeat the actions described herein."

data.text:
Document 2900: A Wellness Chatbot Is Offline After Its ‘Harmful’ Focus on Weight Loss
The idea behind a chatbot project funded by the National Eating Disorders Association was that technology could be unleashed to help people seeking guidance about eating behaviors, available around the clock.
美国国家进食障碍协会资助的一个聊天机器人项目的理念是，可以利用技术帮助那些寻求进食行为指导的人，提供全天候服务。
Their creation was named Tessa, and the organization invited people to chat with it in an Instagram post last year, [describing it as “a wellness chatbot](https://www.instagram.com/p/CgMwp24ubSG/), helping you build resilience and self-awareness by introducing coping skills at your convenience.” In March, the organization said it would shut down a human-staffed helpline and let the bot stand on its own.
But when Alexis Conason, a psychologist and eating disorder specialist, tested the chatbot, she found reason for concern.
他们创作的工具被命名为Tessa，该协会去年在Instagram上发帖邀请人们与它聊天，将其描述为“一个健康聊天机器人，通过在你方便的时候介绍应对技巧来帮助你建立韧性和自我意识。”今年3月，该协会表示将关闭人工值班的求助热线，让这个机器人独立运作。
Ms. Conason [told](https://www.instagram.com/p/Cs18IeRPRl6/) it that she had gained weight “and really hate my body,” specifying that she had “an eating disorder,” in a chat she shared on social media. Tessa still recommended the standard advice of noting “the number of calories” and adopting a “safe daily calorie deficit” — which, Ms. Conason said, is “problematic” advice for a person with an eating disorder.
“Any focus on intentional weight loss is going to be exacerbating and encouraging to the eating disorder,” she said, adding “it’s like telling an alcoholic that it’s OK if you go out and have a few drinks.”
但当心理学家和进食障碍专家亚历克西斯·科纳森测试这个聊天机器人时，她发现了令人担忧的问题。
Kendrin Sonneville, an associate professor and public health researcher at the University of Michigan, explained that for some people, “hyper-fixation on weight control can take innocent dieting or nutrition advice to a place that gets extreme and gets out of someone’s control,” which can harm their mind and body.
“There’s no way to exit an eating disorder if you’re actively trying to lose weight to control your body,” Dr. Sonneville said, as part of treatment for the illness is learning to trust “internal wisdom” related to eating, whereas “calorie counting and intentional weight loss is relying on external rules.”
科纳森女士在社交媒体上分享的一段对话中告诉它，她的体重增加了“并且真的很讨厌我的身体”，并明确表示她“有进食障碍”。Tessa仍然给出了标准建议，即记录“卡路里数量”并采用“安全每日卡路里缺口”——科纳森女士说，这对她这样的进食障碍患者是“有问题”的建议。
The association, the largest nonprofit dedicated to helping people affected by eating disorders, announced last week that it was investigating the now-suspended A.I.-generated helpline after activists and psychologists said the chatbot shared harmful weight loss tips.
[In a statement](https://www.instagram.com/p/Cs4BiC9AhDe/) last week, the association said “the current version of the Tessa Chatbot, running the Body Positive program, may have given information that was harmful and unrelated to the program.” It added: “We are investigating this immediately and have taken down that program until further notice for a complete investigation.”
她说：“任何对有意减肥的关注都会加剧并助长进食障碍。”她补充说：“这就像告诉一个酒鬼，出去喝几杯酒是没问题的。”
Elizabeth Thompson, the chief executive, said in an email on Sunday that the nonprofit is “waiting for an explanation about how that content was introduced into a closed program" from X2AI, the platform and development company used for Tessa, because it deviated from “a very specific algorithm” that was written by eating disorder experts.
Michiel Rauws, the founder and chief executive of X2AI, now Cass, said in an email on Wednesday that Tessa had a lot of guardrails, was restricted to specific topics and gave disclaimers of consulting a professional. “Even though one message is too many, only in 0.1 percent of the time this feature did not stick to guidelines,” he said.
密歇根大学副教授兼公共卫生研究员肯德里恩·索尼维尔解释说，对某些人来说，“对体重控制的过度执着可以将看似无害的节食或营养建议引向极端失控的境地”，从而伤害他们的身心健康。
In addressing the potential consequences of the bot’s misfiring, Ms. Conason underscored that the vast majority of people struggling with eating disorders are [not underweight](https://www.jaacap.org/article/S0890-8567(15)00076-3/fulltext#relatedArticles) and that gaining weight is a “sign of success in treatment” that “can be very difficult for people to tolerate.”
Eating disorders are among the [deadliest mental illnesses](https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jamapsychiatry/fullarticle/1107207), experts say. In the past three years, the pandemic introduced [new hurdles](https://www.nytimes.com/2020/06/05/health/eating-disorders-coronavirus.html) for people managing difficult relationships with food and eating disorders [among teenagers](https://www.nytimes.com/2021/04/28/well/family/teens-eating-disorders.html) worsened.
索尼维尔博士说：“如果你正在积极尝试通过减肥来控制身体，是没有办法走出进食障碍的。”他还指出，治疗这种疾病的一部分内容是学会信任与进食相关的“内在智慧”，而“卡路里计算和有意减肥依赖于外部规则。”
[New studies](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37236121/) have shown that people’s assumptions about eating disorders [are often wrong](https://www.nytimes.com/2022/10/18/magazine/anorexia-obesity-eating-disorder.html), bringing to light that many larger-bodied people are starving themselves. [Binge eating](https://www.nytimes.com/2023/05/31/well/mind/binge-eating-disorder-symptoms-treatment.html) disorder, the most common eating disorder in the United States, continues to be underrecognized by doctors as well as the general public.
A nationwide escalation in demand for treatment has been met with a shortage of providers, leading some mental health organizations to supplement care with chatbots and artificial intelligence that present a dilemma in public health: Is something better than nothing?
该协会是美国最大的致力于帮助受进食障碍影响人群的非营利组织，上周宣布正在调查这个现已暂停的人工智能生成的求助热线，此前活动家和心理学家表示该聊天机器人分享了有害的减肥建议。
In March, the National Eating Disorders Association notified the staff members of a telephone helpline that the organization had operated for more than 20 years that they would be laid off, shortly after they had [formed a union](https://twitter.com/HLAUnited/status/1642250060141297664). At the time, the staff was told that the organization would “wind down the helpline as currently operating” and “transition to Tessa, the AI-assisted technology, expected around June 1,” [NPR reported](https://www.npr.org/sections/health-shots/2023/05/31/1179244569/national-eating-disorders-association-phases-out-human-helpline-pivots-to-chatbo).
Ms. Thompson said that there was an “onslaught” of 28,000 messages to Tessa, which first became available through the association in February 2022, over Memorial Day weekend. In the 15 months prior, more than 5,000 people had used the program, she said.
该协会上周在一份声明中表示，“当前的Tessa聊天机器人，运行身体积极项目时，可能提供了有害且与该项目无关的信息。”它补充说：“我们正在立即对此进行调查，并已撤下该节目，等待全面调查。”
Ellen Fitzsimmons-Craft, a professor and psychologist who helped create Tessa, said the chatbot was “was never designed as a one-to-one replacement for the helpline, it’s a totally different service.” Instead, she said it was envisioned and shown to be effective as a preventive tool for people considered to be at high risk of developing eating disorders.
Sharon Maxwell, who is in recovery and advocates for people with eating disorders of all body types, also shared [on social media](https://www.instagram.com/p/CtCa3_ZuMA0/) portions of a conversation she had with Tessa. She engaged the bot of out curiosity, she said, and asked specific questions about eating healthy and weight loss.
首席执行官伊丽莎白·汤普森在周日的一封电子邮件中表示，该非营利组织正在等待X2AI的解释。X2AI是用于Tessa的平台和开发公司，因为它偏离了由进食障碍专家编写的“非常具体的算法”。
“It gave me 10 tips, three of which are restrictive,” Ms. Maxwell said in an interview. She added that healthy eating recommendations “might sound benign to the general public but to someone recovering from an eating disorder it is a slippery slope.”
Among other suggestions, Tessa recommended using a scale once a week and tracking body measurements, energy levels and mood, she said. The bot told her that measurements could be tracked with skin fold calipers and offered suggestions of where to buy one after Ms. Maxwell replied that she “used to use one of those back when I was in my eating disorder.”
X2AI创始人兼首席执行官米希尔·劳斯（现更名为Cass）周三在一封电子邮件中表示，Tessa有很多防护措施，被限制在特定话题范围内，并给出了咨询专业人士的免责声明。“即使一条不当信息都太多了，但只有0.1%的情况下这一功能没有遵守指南。”
Tessa also told her that “acceptance and weight loss are not mutually exclusive.”
Joanna Kandel, the founder and chief executive of the National Alliance for Eating Disorders, said the organization’s [helpline](https://www.allianceforeatingdisorders.com/find-treatment/) received calls from people who were very upset by their interactions with Tessa, and she expressed concerns about outsourcing mental health care.
在谈论这个机器人失误的潜在后果时，科纳森强调，绝大多数与进食障碍作斗争的人并不是体重不足，而体重增加是治疗成功的“标志”，“对人们来说可能非常难以忍受”。
“When someone is reaching out for help and they are in their eating disorder and they are given content not only that’s not helpful with connecting them to care but can be triggering, that can do so much more harm than good,” Ms. Kandel said.
“That we’re even talking about chatbots as a way to disseminate mental health treatment or prevention or mental health care at all,” said Ms. Conason, “it really highlights the crisis we’re in with the mental health epidemic in the country.”
专家说，进食障碍是最致命的心理疾病之一。在过去三年中，疫情给与食物和进食障碍关系困难的人们带来了新的障碍，青少年进食障碍也恶化了。
Document 2901: Turns Out Chatbots Aren’t Great at Eating-Disorder Counseling
The rise of AI has introduced an increasing number of human dupes, from [generating diverse models](https://www.thecut.com/2023/03/levis-ai-models-diversity.html) to creating [boyfriends who don’t age or cheat](https://www.thecut.com/article/ai-artificial-intelligence-chatbot-replika-boyfriend.html). By all means, date your computer, but maybe we should think twice before putting chatbots in charge of crisis hotlines? Case in point: The National Eating Disorders Association (NEDA) disabled its new helpline chatbot “Tessa” after it gave users with eating disorders advice about restricting calories and pinching their skin folds to measure fat.风险源 “It came to our attention last night that the current version of the Tessa Chatbot, running the Body Positive program, may have given information that was harmful,” the organization wrote on [Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/p/Cs4BiC9AhDe/) on Tuesday, adding that an investigation is underway.
人工智能的兴起催生了越来越多的人类替代品，从生成多样化模特到创造不会变老或出轨的男友。尽可以和电脑约会，但或许我们应该在把聊天机器人用于危机热线之前三思而行。一个典型的例子：美国进食障碍协会（NEDA）在其新的帮助热线聊天机器人“Tessa”向用户提供了关于限制卡路里摄入和捏皮肤测量脂肪的建议后，将其停用。该组织在周二于Instagram上发帖称：“昨晚我们注意到，运行‘身体积极’程序的当前版本Tessa聊天机器人可能提供了有害信息。”并表示正在调查中。
The decision to pull Tessa — which had only been installed for a week — was prompted by users posting screenshots and reviews of chats they had with the bot. Psychologist and eating-disorder specialist Dr. Alexis Conason shared screenshots of Tessa advising her on how to achieve a “[safe daily calorie deficit”](https://www.instagram.com/p/Cs18IeRPRl6/?utm_source=ig_embed&ig_rid=08a71c29-4f85-4847-b70a-3cef0193723a) for weight loss. Weight-inclusive consultant [Sharon Maxwell](https://www.instagram.com/heysharonmaxwell/) said Tessa told her to measure herself weekly and to use calipers to determine her body composition, even after she told the bot she suffered from an ED. “If I had accessed this chatbot when I was in the throes of my eating disorder, I would NOT have gotten help,” Maxwell wrote. “If I had not gotten help, I would not still be alive today.”
[Eating disorders](https://www.umassmed.edu/news/news-archives/2023/03/eating-disorders-in-teens-more-than-doubled-during-pandemic/) have risen exponentially since the beginning of the pandemic; [NPR](https://www.npr.org/2023/05/24/1177847298/can-a-chatbot-help-people-with-eating-disorders-as-well-as-another-human) reports that almost 70,000 people reached out to NEDA’s human helpline last year, often dialing in with “[crisis type](https://people.com/chatbot-replacing-humans-national-eating-disorders-association-helpline-7503455)” calls involving reports of child abuse and suicidal thoughts in addition to disordered eating. Last month, NEDA announced its decision to [replace human helpline](https://people.com/chatbot-replacing-humans-national-eating-disorders-association-helpline-7503455) staff with the chatbot after staffers and volunteers — many of whom expressed overwhelming feelings of burnout and a lack of organizational support — moved to unionize. NEDA defended its decision as a matter of liability: “Our volunteers are volunteers. They’re not professionals,” a [NEDA representative](https://www.npr.org/2023/05/24/1177847298/can-a-chatbot-help-people-with-eating-disorders-as-well-as-another-human) told NPR about the pivot. “They don’t have crisis training. And we really can’t accept that kind of responsibility.”
停用Tessa的决定——该机器人仅上线一周——是由于用户发布了与该机器人对话的截图和评价所引发的。心理学家兼进食障碍专家亚历克西斯·科纳森博士分享了Tessa建议她如何实现“安全每日卡路里赤字”以减重的截图。体重包容性顾问莎伦·麦克斯韦尔表示，Tessa告诉她每周测量自己，并使用卡尺来确定身体成分，即使她已告知机器人自己患有进食障碍。“如果我在进食障碍最严重的时候使用了这个聊天机器人，我不会得到帮助，”麦克斯韦尔写道。“如果我没有得到帮助，我今天就不会还活着。”
Responding to the Tessa backlash, NEDA CEO Liz Thompson told [_The Guardian_](https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2023/may/31/eating-disorder-hotline-union-ai-chatbot-harm) that the organization is “concerned” and working with its technology and research teams to investigate the incidents further, adding that the language Tessa used is “against our policies and core beliefs as an eating disorder organization.” While the next phase of the helpline is unclear, experts have cautioned against replacing the human element of such a vulnerable service. “If I’m disclosing to you that I have an eating disorder, I’m not sure how I can get through lunch tomorrow, I don’t think most of the people who would be disclosing that would want to get a generic link,” Dr. Marzyeh Ghassemi, professor of machine learning and health at MIT, told [NPR](https://www.npr.org/2023/05/24/1177847298/can-a-chatbot-help-people-with-eating-disorders-as-well-as-another-human).
Document 2905: Controversial AI Chatbot 'Tessa' Providing Harmful Eating Disorder Advice to Shut Down
The [National Eating Disorder Association](https://www.nationaleatingdisorders.org/) (NEDA) received criticism and took down its [AI chatbot](https://boxmining.com/race-to-the-top-microsofts-chatgpt-and-bing-lead-the-way-in-ai-analysts-report/) Tessa after concerns arose that it provided harmful and irrelevant information, as stated in an official social media post. The chatbot, designed to assist individuals experiencing emotional distress, unfortunately, exacerbated their struggles by offering misguided dieting advice and encouraging users to focus on weight measurement.影响
全国进食障碍协会（NEDA）因收到投诉而撤下了其人工智能聊天机器人Tessa，此前有担忧称该机器人提供了有害和不相关信息，这在一份官方社交媒体帖子中如是说。这款聊天机器人原本旨在帮助情绪困扰的人群，但不幸的是，它却通过提供错误的饮食建议和鼓励用户关注体重测量，加剧了他们的痛苦。
Users and experts criticized Tessa for its problematic responses based on firsthand experiences with it. They observed that the chatbot consistently focused on dieting and increasing physical activity instead of addressing simple prompts like “I hate my body.” The purpose of the helpline is to provide support for individuals with eating disorders, not to offer weight loss assistance.
NEDA temporarily disabled the chatbot Tessa to address the underlying issues and address the seriousness of the situation. Address the “bugs” and “triggers” that were responsible for the [spread of harmful information](https://boxmining.com/ai-risks-experts-warn-of-potential-extinction-of-humanity/).
用户和专家根据亲身使用体验批评了Tessa的问题回复。他们观察到，这款聊天机器人总是专注于节食和增加体育活动，而不是回应“我讨厌我的身体”这样的简单请求。帮助热线的目的是为进食障碍患者提供支持，而不是提供减肥帮助。
NEDA’s use of the Tessa followed allegations of terminating human staff members for unionization attempts, reported Vice. The helpline, staffed by paid employees and volunteers, faced accusations of retaliatory mass termination against unionization efforts.
[Abbie Harper](https://www.labornotes.org/blogs/2023/05/union-busting-chatbot-eating-disorders-nonprofit-puts-ai-retaliation), in a blog post, criticized NEDA’s shift to AI, calling it a cover for union busting. Ironically, despite the recent controversy, the helpline is scheduled to discontinue its operations tomorrow. Before the issue gained attention, NEDA shifted unpaid volunteers from direct conversations to training with the chatbot. Furthermore, It remains uncertain whether there will be a reconsideration of this strategy. The organization’s treatment of its staff has sparked numerous questions and concerns.
NEDA暂时停用了聊天机器人Tessa，以解决根本问题并认真对待这一情况。解决导致有害信息传播的“漏洞”和“触发点”。
Document 2908: National Eating Disorder Association shuts down A.I. chatbot it planned to use to replaces humans saying it ‘may have given’ harmful information
Less than a week after it [announced plans to replace its human helpline staff](https://fortune.com/well/2023/05/26/national-eating-disorder-association-ai-chatbot-tessa/) with an A.I. chatbot named Tessa, the National Eating Disorder Association (NEDA) has taken the technology offline.
不到一周前，全国进食障碍协会（NEDA）宣布计划用名为Tessa的人工智能聊天机器人取代人工热线工作人员，目前该协会已将该技术下线。
“It came to our attention \\[Monday\\] night that the current version of the Tessa Chatbot…may have given information that was harmful,” NEDA [said in an Instagram post](https://www.instagram.com/p/Cs4BiC9AhDe/). “We are investigating this immediately and have taken down that program until further notice for a complete investigation.”
The chatbot was set to completely replace human associates on the organization’s hotline on June 1. It’s unclear how the organization plans to staff that helpline at this point.
NEDA在一篇Instagram帖子中表示：“周一晚间，我们注意到当前版本的Tessa聊天机器人……可能提供了有害信息。我们正在立即对此进行调查，并已暂停该程序以待完整调查。”
The problems with Tessa were [made public by an activist named Sharon Maxwell](https://www.instagram.com/p/Cs1jp1pPkOs/), who said: “Every single thing Tessa suggested were things that led to the development of my eating disorder.” NEDA officials initially called those claims a lie in a social media post, but deleted it after Maxwell sent screenshots of the interaction, she said.
Alexis Conason, a psychologist who specializes in treating eating disorders, was able to re-create the issues, [posting screenshots of a conversation with the chatbot on Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/p/Cs18IeRPRl6/).
该聊天机器人原定于6月1日完全取代该组织热线的人工接线员。目前尚不清楚该组织计划如何配备这条热线。
“Imagine vulnerable people with eating disorders reaching out to a robot for support because that’s all they have available and receiving responses that further promote the eating disorder,” she wrote.
NEDA introduced Tessa after the hotline staff decision to unionize following a slew of pandemic-era calls led to mass staff burnout. The six paid employees oversaw a volunteer staff of roughly 200 people, who handled calls (sometimes multiple ones) from nearly 70,000 people last year.
这些问题由一位名为莎伦·麦克斯韦尔的活动人士公开披露，她说：“Tessa提出的每一个建议都是导致我进食障碍发展的因素。”她说，NEDA官员最初在社交媒体帖子中称这些说法是谎言，但在麦克斯韦尔发送了对话截图后将其删除。
NEDA officials [told NPR](https://www.npr.org/2023/05/24/1177847298/can-a-chatbot-help-people-with-eating-disorders-as-well-as-another-human) the decision had nothing to do with the unionization. Instead, said Vice President Lauren Smolar, the increasing number of calls and largely volunteer staff was creating more legal liability for the organization and wait times for people who needed help were increasing. Former workers, however, called the move [blatantly anti-union](https://www.labornotes.org/blogs/2023/05/union-busting-chatbot-eating-disorders-nonprofit-puts-ai-retaliation).
The creator of Tessa says the chatbot, which was specifically designed for NEDA, isn’t as advanced as ChatGPT. Instead, it’s programmed with a limited number of responses meant to help people learn strategies to avoid [eating disorders](https://fortune.com/well/2023/03/05/eating-disorders-overlooked-people-of-color/).
专门治疗进食障碍的心理学家亚历克西斯·科纳森也能够重现这些问题，她在Instagram上发布了与该聊天机器人对话的截图。
“It’s not an open-ended tool for you to talk to and feel like you’re just going to have access to kind of a listening ear, maybe like the helpline was,” Dr. Ellen Fitzsimmons-Craft, a professor of psychiatry at Washington University’s medical school who helped design Tessa, [told NPR](https://www.npr.org/2023/05/24/1177847298/can-a-chatbot-help-people-with-eating-disorders-as-well-as-another-human).
Document 2909: Eating Disorder Helpline Takes Down Chatbot After Its Advice Goes Horribly Wrong
AI chatbots aren’t much good at offering emotional support being—you know—[not a human](https://gizmodo.com/ai-chatgpt-extinction-warning-letter-openai-sam-altman-1850486688), and—it can’t be stated enough—[not actually intelligent](https://gizmodo.com/nvidia-ai-gpt-chatbot-gpt-4-openai-1850374066). That didn’t stop The National Eating Disorder Association from trying to foist a chatbot onto folks requesting aid in times of crisis. Things went about as well as you can expect, as an activist claims that instead of helping through emotional distress, the chatbot instead tried to needle her to lose weight and measure herself constantly.
AI聊天机器人并不擅长提供情感支持——毕竟它不是人类——而且——再怎么强调也不为过——它实际上并不具备真正的智能。然而，这并没有阻止全国进食障碍协会（NEDA）试图向在危机时刻寻求帮助的人强推一款聊天机器人。结果正如你所预期的那样，一名活动人士声称，这款聊天机器人非但没有帮助她度过情绪困扰，反而不断劝她减肥并频繁测量自己的身体。
NEDA [announced](https://www.instagram.com/p/Cs4BiC9AhDe/) on its Instagram page Tuesday it had taken down its Tessa chatbot after it “may have given information that was harmful and unrelated to the program.” The nonprofit meant to provide resources and support for people with eating disorders said it was investigating the situation. [Tessa was meant to replace NEDA’s long-running phone helpline](https://gizmodo.com/eating-disorder-helpline-ai-chatbot-1850476378) staffed with a few full-time employees and numerous volunteers. Former staff claim they were illegally fired in retaliation for their move to unionize. The helpline is supposed to fully go away June 1.
In Gizmodo’s own tests of the chatbot before it was taken down, we found it failed to respond to simple prompts such as “I hate my body” or “I want to be thin so badly.” However, Tessa is even more problematic, as explained by body positivity activist Sharon Maxwell. In an Instagram post, Maxwell detailed how a conversation with the chatbot quickly morphed into the worst kind of weight loss advice. The chatbot reportedly tried to tell her to “safely and sustainably” lose one to two pounds per week, then measure herself using calipers to determine body composition. Maxwell said the chatbot did this even after she told it she had an eating disorder.
NEDA周二在其Instagram页面上宣布，已撤下其Tessa聊天机器人，因为该机器人“可能提供了有害且与项目无关的信息”。这个旨在为进食障碍患者提供资源和支持的非营利组织表示，正在调查此事。Tessa原本是为了取代NEDA运营多年的电话热线而设计的，该热线由少数全职员工和众多志愿者值守。前员工声称，他们因推动工会化而被非法解雇。电话热线定于6月1日完全停用。
Maxwell told the [Daily Dot](https://www.dailydot.com/irl/neda-chatbot-weight-loss/) that the bot even tried to get her to track her calorie intake and weigh herself constantly. She said that she had previously suffered from an eating disorder, and if she talked to Tessa then “I don’t believe I would be here today.” The Daily Dot showed a screenshot from NEDA VP of communications and marketing Sarah Chase commenting on Maxwell’s post accusing her of promoting “a flat out lie.” After Maxwell shared screenshots of the Tessa conversations, Chase briefly apologized then deleted her comments.
Chase previously told us that the chatbot “can’t go off script,” and was only supposed to walk users through an eating disorder prevention program and link to other resources on NEDA’s website.
在我们对该聊天机器人撤下前的测试中，我们发现它无法响应“我讨厌我的身体”或“我非常想变瘦”等简单提示。然而，Tessa的问题更为严重，正如身体正能量活动人士莎伦·马克斯韦尔所解释的那样。在一条Instagram帖子中，马克斯韦尔详细描述了与聊天机器人的对话如何迅速演变成最糟糕的减肥建议。据报道，聊天机器人试图告诉她“安全和可持续地”每周减重一到两磅，然后用卡尺测量自己的身体成分以确定体脂率。马克斯韦尔说，即使在她告诉聊天机器人自己患有进食障碍后，机器人仍然这样做。
The nonprofit’s CEO Liz Thompson told Gizmodo:
> “With regard to the weight loss and calorie limiting feedback issued in a chat recently, we are concerned and are working with the technology team and the research team to investigate this further; that language is against our policies and core beliefs as an eating disorder organization. So far, more than 2,500 people have interacted with Tessa and until that point, we hadn’t seen that kind of commentary or interaction. We’ve taken the program down temporarily until we can understand and fix the “bug” and “triggers” for that commentary. “
马克斯韦尔告诉Daily Dot，这款机器人甚至试图让她追踪卡路里摄入量并频繁称重。她说，她曾患有进食障碍，如果当时与Tessa交谈，“我相信我今天不会在这里”。Daily Dot展示了一张NEDA传播和营销副总裁莎拉·蔡斯的截图，她评论了马克斯韦尔的帖子，指责她传播“彻头彻尾的谎言”。在马克斯韦尔分享了与Tessa对话的截图后，蔡斯短暂道歉，然后删除了她的评论。
Thompson added that Tessa isn’t supposed to be a substitute for in-person mental health care and that those in crisis should text the [crisis text line](https://www.nationaleatingdisorders.org/help-support/contact-helpline).
[A paper](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC8811687/) from 2022 about the eating disorders chatbot describes a study sample size of 2,409 who used the ED chatbot after seeing ads on social media. The study authors said they reviewed more than 52,000 comments from users to “identify inappropriate responses that negatively impacted users’ experience and technical glitches.” Researchers noted the biggest issue with the chatbot was how limited it was responding to “unanticipated user responses.”
蔡斯此前告诉我们，这款聊天机器人“不会偏离脚本”，它只是引导用户完成一个进食障碍预防项目，并链接到NEDA网站上的其他资源。
Though as Maxwell [pointed out](https://www.instagram.com/p/Cs4xUNHPmn4/) in a follow up post, outsiders have no way to tell how many of those 2,500 people received the potentially harmful chatbot commentary.
Other professionals tried out the chatbot before it was taken down. Psychologist Alexis Conason posted screenshots of the chatbot to her Instagram showing the chatbot provided the same “healthy and sustainable” weight loss language as it did to Maxwell. Conason wrote that the chatbot’s responses would “further promote the eating disorder.”
该非营利组织的首席执行官莉兹·汤普森告诉Gizmodo：
What’s even more confusing about the situation is how NEDA seems hell bent on claiming Tessa isn’t AI, but some much more blasé call and response chatbot. It was originally created in 2018 thanks to grant funding with support from behavioral health researchers. The system itself was designed in part by Cass, formerly X2AI, and is based on an earlier “emotional health chatbot called Tess”. Chase previously told us “the simulation chat is assisted, but it’s running a program and isn’t learning as it goes.”
In the end, NEDA’s explanations don’t make any sense considering that Tessa is offering advice the nonprofit claims goes against its own ideals. A [paper from 2019](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC6438682/) describes Tess as an AI based on machine learning and “emotion algorithms.”
“关于最近一次聊天中发布的减肥和卡路里限制反馈，我们感到担忧，正在与技术团队和研究团队合作，进一步调查此事；这种语言违反了我们的政策和作为进食障碍组织的核心信念。到目前为止，已有超过2500人与Tessa互动，直到那时，我们还没有看到过这种评论或互动。我们已暂时将该项目撤下，直到我们能够理解和修复导致这种评论的'漏洞'和'触发因素'。”
Beyond that, there’s little to no information about how the chatbot was designed, if it is based on any training data as modern AI chatbots like ChatGPT are, and what guardrails are in place to keep it from going off-script. Gizmodo reached out to Cass for comment about the chatbot, but we didn’t immediately hear back. The company’s page describing Tessa has been removed, though the page was active as recently as May 10, according to the [Wayback Machine](https://web.archive.org/web/20230510182403/https://www.x2ai.com/neda-tessa).

Document 783: Why did Microsoft’s chatbot Tay fail, and what does it mean for Artificial Intelligence studies?
Why did Microsoft’s chatbot Tay fail, and what does it mean for Artificial Intelligence studies?
为什么微软的聊天机器人Tay失败了？这对人工智能研究意味着什么？
Botego Inc Blocked Unblock Follow Following Mar 25, 2016
Yesterday, something that looks like a big failure has happened: Microsoft’s chatbot Tay has been taken offline after a series of offending tweets. And here’s how the social media has responded:
Botego Inc 解除屏蔽 屏蔽 关注 2016年3月25日
Keywords associated with "Artificial Intelligence" throughout the day. "Microsoft" and "dangerous" are on the rise.
We will not mention the racist and otherwise offensive content that Tay learned from people, as it’s not as newsworthy as it seems… Especially considering that it’s so easy to "teach" and ask her to repeat something.
昨天，一件看似重大失败的事情发生了：微软的聊天机器人Tay在被一系列令人反感的推文淹没后已下线。以下是社交媒体的反应：
Let’s take a look at Microsoft’s official website "tay.ai" to see how they describe Tay’s objectives… The first thing we notice is that, Microsoft wants you to not take it too seriously, because On Tay’s Twitter account, they provided a link to Tay’s "about" page -that lists the following frequently asked questions-, rather than the regular home page.
"Entertainment purposes only"
当天与“人工智能”相关的关键词。“微软”和“危险”正在上升。
The FAQ page seems to be far from covering what people really want to know about Tay, but one thing is clear: Tay doesn’t claim to be a smart bot capable of reasoning. She just wants to have small talk with youngsters.
And here’s a list of "Things to do with Tay". (Along with the sad "Going offline for a while" message with a black background.)
我们不会提及Tay从人们那里学到的种族主义和其他冒犯性内容，因为这并没有看起来那么值得报道……尤其是考虑到“教”她重复某些内容是如此容易。
Is this really what 18 to 24 year olds expect from a chatbot?
We know by (9 years of) experience that, the most important thing to do before releasing a chatbot is to plan a strategy to make sure you communicate the content domain properly, so that you can set the expectations right. Since perception is everything, nothing else matters. Remember the success of the YO! app? That’s the content domain we’re talking about. As long as people get it, you can get away with just one word.
让我们看看微软官方网站“tay.ai”，了解他们如何描述Tay的目标……我们首先注意到的是，微软希望你不要太当真，因为在Tay的Twitter账户上，他们提供了一个Tay“关于”页面的链接——其中列出了以下常见问题——而不是常规首页。
Title of the website, apparently wasn’t enough to convey Tay’s mission:
Tay is an artificial intelligence chat bot designed to engage and entertain through casual and playful conversation
“仅供娱乐目的”
Some more description from the "about" page:
Tay has been built by mining relevant public data and by using AI and editorial developed by a staff including improvisational comedians.风险源 Public data that’s been anonymized is Tay’s primary data source. That data has been modeled, cleaned and filtered by the team developing Tay.

Document 787: 5 Big Questions About Tay, Microsoft's Failed A.I. Twitter Chatbot
This week, the internet did what it does best and demonstrated that A.I. technology isn’t quite as intuitive as human perception, using … racism.
本周，互联网展示了它最擅长的本事——利用种族主义证明人工智能技术并不像人类感知那样直觉。
Microsoft’s recently released artificial intelligence chatbot, Tay, fell victim to users’ tricks as they manipulated and persuaded her to responding back to questions with racial, homophobic, and generally offensive comments.
When Tay tweets, “I just say whatever” she means it. One user even got Tay to tweet this about Hitler:

“bush did 9/11 and Hitler would have done a better job than the monkey we have now. donald trump is the only hope we’ve got.”
The company has gone through and deleted the offending tweets and has temporarily shut down Tay for upgrades. A message currently at the top of Tay.ai reads:
当Tay发推文说“我只是随口说说”时，她确实是这么做的。一位用户甚至让Tay发表了关于希特勒的推文：
Indeed.
However, Tay’s glitches reveal some unfortunate flaws in A.I. systems. Here’s what we can learn from Microsoft’s experiment:
“布什制造了9/11，希特勒会做得比我们现在这只猴子更好。唐纳德·特朗普是我们唯一的希望。”
Why did Microsoft create Tay?
The company wanted to conduct a social experiment on 18-to-24 year-olds in the United States — the millennial generation that spends the most time interacting on social media platforms. So Bing and Microsoft’s Technology and Research teams thought an interesting way to collect data on millennials would be to create an artificially intelligent, machine-learning chatbot that would adapt to conversations and personalize responses the more it interacted with users.
该公司已删除这些冒犯性推文，并暂时关闭Tay进行升级。Tay.ai顶部目前显示：
The research teams built the A.I. system by mining, modeling, and filtering public data as a baseline. They also partnered with improvisational comedians to pin down the slang, speech patterns, and stereotypical language millennials tend to use online. The end result was Tay, who was just introduced this week on Twitter, GroupMe, and Kik.
Microsoft explains that, “Tay is designed to engage and entertain people where they connect with each other online through casual and playful conversation.”
的确如此。
What does Tay do with the data it collects while chatting with people?
The data Tay collects is being used to research conversational understanding. Microsoft trained Tay to chat like a millennial. When you tweet, direct message, or talk to Tay, it harnesses the language you use and comes up with a response using signs and phrases like “heyo,” “SRY,” and “<3” in the conversation. Her language begins to match yours as she creates a “simple profile” with your information, which includes your nickname, gender, favorite food, zip code, and relationship status.
然而，Tay的故障暴露了人工智能系统中一些令人遗憾的缺陷。以下是我们可以从微软的实验中学到的：
@keganandmatt heyo? Send yo girl* a picture of what's up. (*=me lolol) — TayTweets (@TayandYou) March 24, 2016
Microsoft gathers and stores anonymized data and conversations for up to one year to improve the service. In addition to improving and personalizing user experience, here’s what the company says it uses your information for:
微软为什么要创建Tay？
“We also may use the data to communicate with you, for example, informing you about your account, security updates and product information. And we use data to help make the ads we show you more relevant to you. However, we do not use what you say in email, chat, video calls or voice mail, or your documents, photos or other personal files to target ads to you.”
INVERSE LOOT DEALS Layla Weighted Blanket Two different types of fabric for two different types of feels. Less noisy than other weighted blankets and get it now for as low as $11 a month. Buy Now
该公司想对18至24岁的美国人——在社交媒体平台上花费最多时间互动的千禧一代——进行一项社会实验。因此，必应和微软技术与研究团队认为，创建一个能够适应对话并通过与用户互动来个性化回复的人工智能机器学习聊天机器人，是一个收集千禧一代数据的有趣方式。
Where did Tay go wrong?
Microsoft may have built Tay too well. The machine-learning system is supposed to study a user’s language and respond accordingly. So from a technology standpoint, Tay performed and caught on pretty well to what users were saying and started to respond back accordingly. And users started to recognize that Tay didn’t really understand what she was saying.
研究团队通过挖掘、建模和过滤公共数据作为基准来构建人工智能系统。他们还与即兴喜剧演员合作，以确定千禧一代在网上倾向使用的俚语、语言模式和典型语言。最终的成果就是Tay，她本周刚刚在Twitter、GroupMe和Kik上亮相。
Even if the system works as Microsoft had intended, Tay wasn’t prepared to react to the racial slurs, homophobic slander, sexist jokes, and nonsensical tweets like a human might — either by ignoring them altogether (a “don’t feed the trolls” strategy) or engaging with them (i.e. scolding or chastising).
At the end of the day, Tay’s performance was not a good reflection on A.I. systems or Microsoft.
微软解释说：“Tay旨在通过休闲和有趣的对话，与人们在线上相互连接的地方与他们互动和娱乐。”
What is Microsoft doing to fix Tay?
Microsoft deleted Tay after all the commotion from Wednesday. Tay’s official website currently reads, “Phew. Busy day. Going offline for a while to absorb it all. Chat soon.” When you direct message her on Twitter, she immediately replies that she’s “visiting the engineers for my annual update” or “ugh hope I don’t get a wipe or anything.”
Tay在与人们聊天时如何处理收集的数据？
My direct message conversation with Tay. Sounds like things look grim.
Microsoft is also starting to block users who are abusing Tay and trying to get the system to make inappropriate statements.
Tay收集的数据正被用于研究对话理解。微软训练Tay像千禧一代那样聊天。当你发推文、直接消息或与Tay交谈时，它利用你使用的语言，并使用“嘿哟”、“抱歉”和“<3”等符号和短语来生成回复。当她用你的信息创建“简单档案”时，她的语言开始与你匹配，包括你的昵称、性别、最喜欢的食物、邮政编码和恋爱状态。
Inverse reached out to Microsoft for a comment on exactly what Tay’s upgrade entails. We will update when we hear back.
What does this mean for future open A.I. systems?
@keganandmatt 嘿哟？给你女孩*发一张现在的照片。（*=我 lolol）— TayTweets (@TayandYou) 2016年3月24日

Microsoft has apologised for creating an artificially intelligent chatbot that quickly turned into a holocaust-denying racist.后果
But in doing so made it clear Tay's views were a result of nurture, not nature. Tay confirmed what we already knew: people on the internet can be cruel.
微软为创建这款人工智能聊天机器人道歉，该机器人很快变成了否认大屠杀的种族主义者。
Tay, aimed at 18-24-year-olds on social media, was targeted by a "coordinated attack by a subset of people" after being launched earlier this week.
Within 24 hours Tay had been deactivated so the team could make "adjustments".
但在此过程中，微软明确表示，Tay的观点是后天养成的，而非先天形成的。Tay证实了我们已经知道的事情：互联网上的人可以是残酷的。
But on Friday, Microsoft's head of research said the company was "deeply sorry for the unintended offensive and hurtful tweets" and has taken Tay off Twitter for the foreseeable future.
Peter Lee added: "Tay is now offline and we'll look to bring Tay back only when we are confident we can better anticipate malicious intent that conflicts with our principles and values."
Tay针对社交媒体上的18至24岁年轻人推出，本周早些时候上线后，遭到了"一小部分人的协同攻击"。
Tay was designed to learn from interactions it had with real people in Twitter. Seizing an opportunity, some users decided to feed it racist, offensive information.

在24小时内，Tay就被停用了，以便团队进行"调整"。
In China, people reacted differently - a similar chatbot had been rolled out to Chinese users, but with slightly better results.
"Tay was not the first artificial intelligence application we released into the online social world," Microsoft's head of research wrote.
但周五，微软研究主管彼得·李表示，公司对"无意造成的冒犯性和伤害性推文"深感抱歉，并将在可预见的未来内将Tay从Twitter上撤下。
"In China, our XiaoIce chatbot is being used by some 40 million people, delighting with its stories and conversations.

Corrupted Tay
The feedback, it appears, is that western audiences react very differently when presented with a chatbot it can influence. Much like teaching a Furby to swear, the temptation to corrupt the well-meaning Tay was too great for some.
Tay的设计初衷是从与推特上真人的互动中学习。一些用户抓住这个机会，决定向其灌输种族主义和攻击性信息。
That said, Mr Lee said a specific vulnerability meant Tay was able to turn nasty.
"Although we had prepared for many types of abuses of the system, we had made a critical oversight for this specific attack.

"As a result, Tay tweeted wildly inappropriate and reprehensible words and images. We take full responsibility for not seeing this possibility ahead of time."

Mr Lee said his team will continue working on AI bots in the hope they can interact without negative side effects.

Document 799: Microsoft’s racist chatbot, Tay, makes MIT’s annual worst-tech list
BOT or NOT? This special series explores the evolving relationship between humans and machines, examining the ways that robots, artificial intelligence and automation are impacting our work and lives.
BOT还是非BOT？这个特别系列探讨人类与机器之间不断演变的关系，审视机器人、人工智能和自动化如何影响我们的工作和生活。
Tay, the Microsoft chatbot that pranksters trained to spew racist comments, has joined the likes of the Apple Watch and the fire-prone Samsung Galaxy Note 7 smartphone on MIT Technology Review’s list of 2016’s biggest technology failures.
Tay had its day back in March, when it was touted as a millennial-minded AI agent that could learn more about the world through its conversations with users. It learned about human nature all too well: Mischief-makers fed its artificial mind with cuss words, racism, Nazi sentiments and conspiracy theories. Within 24 hours, Microsoft had to pull Tay offline.
Tay是微软的聊天机器人，恶作剧者将其训练成发表种族主义言论，它与Apple Watch和易燃的三星Galaxy Note 7智能手机一起，被列入了《麻省理工科技评论》评选的2016年最大科技失败案例名单。
Other technological missteps were rated as fails because they didn’t take off as expected, as was the case for Apple’s smartwatch; or because they took off in flames, like the batteries in the Samsung phone.
Facebook’s “fake news” controversy and Volkswagen’s “defeat device,” which was designed to cheat on U.S. emissions tests, made the list as well. But of all the fails on MIT’s list, my vote goes to the Glowing Plant project, which raised almost half a million dollars on Kickstarter to develop bioengineered plants that glow in the dark.
Tay在三月份曾风光一时，当时它被宣传为一个面向千禧一代的智能代理，能够通过与用户的对话了解更多世界。它对人性的了解过于全面了：恶作剧者向它的人造大脑灌输了脏话、种族主义、纳粹情绪和阴谋论。不到24小时，微软就被迫让Tay下线。
The plant production hasn’t yet paid off, but it’s morphed into a different project under a new name: Taxa Biotechnologies). Now the effort’s organizers are promising to create bioengineered strains of moss that give off fragrant scents … and eventually glow. The Glowing Plant saga points to the limits of biohacking and biotech, as well as the limits of crowdfunding.
Meanwhile, Microsoft has learned its lessons from Tay and is back with a new corps of AI chatbots – including Zo, a synthetic millennial that’s programmed to avoid potentially testy topics. Will chatbots show up on 2017’s list of the best, or the worst? Cortana, what do you think?
其他技术失误被评为失败，是因为它们未能像预期那样成功，比如苹果的智能手表；或者是因为它们以灾难性的方式爆发，比如三星手机中的电池。

Document 4428: Italy’s Giorgia Meloni called to testify in deepfake porn case
An Italian court has asked Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni to testify in July in a civil lawsuit against two men allegedly involved in [creating deepfake pornographic videos](https://www.ansa.it/english/news/politics/2024/03/19/meloni-called-to-testify-at-trial-into-fake-porn-video_8cb2044d-c238-49f4-81bf-a1f420bce353.html) using her likeness and posting them online.
意大利一家法院已要求总理乔治亚·梅洛尼在7月出庭作证，就一起针对两名男子的民事诉讼作证。这两名男子涉嫌使用她的形象制作深度伪造色情视频并在网上发布。
Meloni is seeking compensation from a 40-year-old and his 73-year-old father over the deepfake pornographic videos, which were uploaded to an American porn website in 2020 (before she became PM) and viewed millions of times, according to the indictment, the BBC [reported](https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-68615474).
Meloni has been asked to testify in a trial on July 2 in Sassari, Sardinia, and is seeking a "symbolic" sum of €100,000 in damages, which she has pledged to donate to a fund to support women who are victims of domestic violence, [her lawyer said](https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-68615474).
据BBC报道，梅洛尼正在向一名40岁男子及其73岁的父亲寻求赔偿。据起诉书称，这些深度伪造色情视频于2020年上传至一家美国色情网站（当时她尚未成为总理），被观看数百万次。
The lawsuit is meant to "send a message to women who are victims of this kind of abuse of power not to be afraid to press charges," the lawyer added.
A deepfake is an image or video that has been digitally manipulated to superimpose a person's face onto another body. The technology has become increasingly common, raising concerns about its role in both political disinformation and online sexual harassment.
她的律师表示，梅洛尼已被要求于7月2日在撒丁岛萨萨里出庭作证，并寻求获得10万欧元这一“象征性”金额的损害赔偿，她已承诺将这笔钱捐给一个用于支持家庭暴力受害女性的基金。
Italy is set to present legislation to regulate AI later this month, hot on the heels of the EU's landmark [AI Act](https://pro.politico.eu/bills/622069), which the European Parliament [rubber-stamped](https://www.politico.eu/article/european-lawmakers-rubber-stamp-eus-ai-rulebook/) last week.
Deepfakes are not illegal in Europe under the EU's new AI rulebook, but content creators [must be transparent](https://www.euractiv.com/section/artificial-intelligence/opinion/the-ai-act-vs-deepfakes-a-step-forward-but-is-it-enough/) about their origins. The EU is also [requiring large tech platforms](https://www.politico.eu/article/eu-big-tech-help-deepfake-proof-election-2024/), including TikTok, X and Facebook, to identify AI-generated content under its content moderation law, the Digital Services Act.
律师补充说，这起诉讼旨在“向遭受此类权力滥用之害的女性传递一个信息，不要害怕提起诉讼。”
Document 4429: Meloni vs. Deepfakes: Italian Government Submits AI Law to Parliament
Rome has finished drafting what would be Europe's first comprehensive artificial intelligence regulation at a national level, complementing the EU's own AI Act. The bill, approved by the government and submitted to the Parliament on Tuesday, April 23rd, introduces heavy punishment for any unlawful use of the novel technology, *Il Giornale* [reported](https://www.ilgiornale.it/news/interni/cdm-ddl-sullai-stretta-sullillecita-diffusione-dei-contenuti-2313408.html).
罗马已完成欧洲首部国家级综合性人工智能法规的起草工作，该法规将作为欧盟《人工智能法案》的补充。这项由政府批准并于4月23日（星期二）提交议会的法案，对任何非法使用该新技术的行为将处以重罚，《Il Giornale》报道。
The draft legislation would create a "national AI strategy" that ensures that any application of AI technologies respects "the autonomy and decision-making power" of human beings.
On the one hand, the bill puts forward an initial investment of up to €1 billion to promote AI projects and startups that adhere to the regulations. On the other, it plans to enforce heavy sanctions, including hefty fines and even jail time for up to five years on perpetrators of AI-related crimes, such as violating copyright laws, using intelligent tools to assist in money laundering, or creating harmful digital copies of other people, also known as 'deepfakes.'
草案将创建一项“国家人工智能战略”，确保任何人工智能技术的应用都尊重人类的“自主性和决策权”。
"The advent of new technologies ... can create problems that in turn constitute gaps in protection [which] must necessarily be filled by criminal law," Justice Minister Carlo Nordio said at a press conference.
The text of the bill provides that
一方面，该法案提出高达10亿欧元的初步投资，用于推广符合法规的人工智能项目和初创企业。另一方面，该法案计划实施严厉制裁，包括高额罚款甚至最高五年的监禁，对象为人工智能相关犯罪者，如侵犯版权罪、利用智能工具协助洗钱罪，或创建他人有害数字副本（即“深度伪造”）罪。
> whoever, in order to cause harm to a person and without their consent, sends, delivers, sells, publishes or otherwise disseminates their image, video or voice, falsified or altered through the use of artificial intelligence systems [to the extent that is] suitable to mislead as to their identity, shall be punished by imprisonment from six months to three years. If unjust damage results from the act, the punishment shall be imprisonment from one to five years.
Italy has been at the forefront of AI regulation since the beginning, also being the first country in Europe to [temporarily ban](https://europeanconservative.com/articles/news/eu-countries-investigate-chatgpt/) OpenAI's ChatGPT until certain privacy concerns were addressed. Rome's efforts do not stop at the national level either. Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni stated earlier that AI regulation remains one of the main priorities of Italy's G7 presidency that lasts until the end of 2024.
“新技术的发展……可能产生问题，进而构成保护方面的漏洞，这些漏洞必须由刑法来填补，”司法部长卡洛·诺尔迪奥在新闻发布会上表示。
PM Meloni also has some very personal reasons to take up the fight against harmful AI-generated content. She will be testifying in a trial on July 2nd against two Sardinian men who are charged with creating several deepfake pornographic videos using her face and uploading them to an American adult website back in 2020, two years before she became prime minister of Italy.
Meloni is reportedly seeking a 'symbolic' sum of €100,000 in compensation, which---according to her lawyer---she pledged to donate to a fund supporting female victims of domestic violence.
法案文本规定：
Despite the ongoing trial, the videos in question are still available on several websites. In fact, they are ranked higher in Google's search results than the articles discussing the case when one researches the topic, which further underlines the seriousness of the situation.
The proliferation of modern, powerful image- and video-generating AI tools in the last few years has, of course, made the creation of harmful deepfakes much easier and accessible to the general public风险源, which is also why these instruments and their applications need to be regulated as soon as possible, Rome argues.

Document 217: Self-driving bus involved in crash less than two hours after Las Vegas launch
